rejected.title: Sectors of the economy
card: Households
people who live in one home, alone or together. They sell their labour, buy goods and services, and may save.
Businesses
make and sell goods and services. They buy resources and hire workers.
Financial sector
banks and similar organisations. Banks are businesses, but they are grouped as their own sector because they take savings from some people and lend money to others.
Government
collects taxes and provides services such as roads and public schools. It also buys goods and services.
rejected.remember: Households, businesses, the financial sector and government each play a different part in the market.

a.q: A bank pays interest on savings and lends a family money to buy a home. In the four-sector model, which sector is the bank in?
a.why: Banks take in savings and lend money out, so they are grouped as the financial sector. A bank is a kind of business, but in this model it is placed in its own sector, not with other businesses.
a.clue: Which sector is set apart for saving and lending?

b.q: A council in Tasmania collects rates, a local tax, and uses them to repair a local road. Which sector does this show?
opts: Government, which taxes and provides services
Households, which sell labour for income
Businesses, which make goods to sell
Financial sector, which lends savings to others
b.why: Collecting tax from people and spending it on a road is what government does. The council might pay a business to do the repair, but the council doing the taxing and providing the road is government.
b.clue: Who collects taxes and provides roads?

a.q: A bank pays interest on savings and lends money to a family to buy a home. Which sector is the bank in?
a.why: Banks take in savings and lend money out, which is the work of the financial sector. A family is a household, but the bank is not one.
a.clue: Think about who saves and lends money.

a.q: A credit union holds its members' savings and lends money to members buying cars. Which of the four sectors is it in?
a.why: A credit union takes in savings and lends money out, as a bank does, so it is grouped in the financial sector. It is run like a business, but in this model saving and lending organisations have a sector of their own.
a.clue: Which sector is set apart for saving and lending?

b.q: A council in Tasmania charges rates on local land and pays a building firm to fix a road for residents. Which sector is the council in?
b.why: Rates are a tax, and collecting tax to provide a road is what government does. The building firm that does the work is a business, but the council that charges the rates and provides the road is government.
b.clue: Who collects the money and decides the road gets fixed?
